sources.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy)

read_evidence.method: The complete PDF (706,612 bytes) was downloaded and extracted to text; the named results of Sections 8.1-8.6 and the displayed proofs of the degree shift, Riemann's theorem, the canonical-divisor corollary and the Riemann-Roch theorem were read against the batch-7 inventory.
read_evidence.scope: Chapter 8, Sections 8.1-8.6, all named results and their proofs

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 3(3)-(4): l(D) is finite dimensional and depends only on the linear equivalence class of D
Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 3(1)-(2): D <= D' gives L(D) contained in L(D'); dim L(D')/L(D) <= deg(D'-D); L(0)=k and L(D)=0 for deg D<0
Ch. 8 §8.2 Lemma 1: for finite S, dim(L_S(D')/L_S(D)) = deg_S(D'-D)
Ch. 8 §8.3 Riemann's theorem: there is an integer g with l(D) >= deg(D)+1-g for every divisor D; the smallest such g is the genus
Ch. 8 §8.3 Examples(1) and the Corollary to Proposition 4 of §8.2: g=0 if and only if the curve is rational, equivalently isomorphic to P^1, equivalently l(P)>1 for some P
Ch. 8 §8.4 Proposition 6: the module of differentials of a one-variable function field is one dimensional over the field
contents.reason: The one-dimensionality of the differential module is canonical-divisor machinery that this page never uses; the torsion-free/locally-free lemma is backed by Artin 8.1.1 instead, and the differentials belong to the duality pair.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.6 Riemann-Roch theorem, Euler-characteristic content: chi(O(D)) = deg(D) + 1 - g (proved via the degree shift from O)
Ch. 8 §8.6 Riemann-Roch theorem: l(D) = deg(D) + 1 - g + l(W-D) for a canonical divisor W
contents.reason: This page proves the same identity in Euler-characteristic form, l(D) - i(D) = deg(D) + 1 - g (thm-riemann-roch-as-l-minus-index); the l(W-D) form of the statement is the Serre-duality identification of i(D), which the duality pair proves.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.6 Noether's reduction lemma: if l(D)>0 and l(W-D-P) differs from l(W-D) then l(D+P)=l(D) (the comparison step behind the degree shift)
Ch. 8 §8.6 Proposition 9: the speciality delta(D) equals l(W-D) (duality statement, used here only as the classical name of the unknown defect)
contents.reason: The identification of the index of speciality with l(W-D) is exactly Serre duality, which this page does not use; def-index-speciality-divisor only borrows the classical name for i(D) = h^1(C, O_C(D)).

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.6 Corollary 1: l(W) = g for a canonical divisor (extracted only after duality; the Euler-characteristic content 1-g = chi(O) is used on this page)
contents.reason: l(W) = g is a canonical-bundle section count, the h^0 half of Serre duality; this page uses only the Euler-characteristic normalisation chi(O_C) = 1 - g, which def-genus-euler-characteristic-curve records.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.1 Corollaries 1-2: div(z) >= 0 forces z in k, and div(z)=div(z') if and only if z' is a scalar multiple of z
Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 3(2) and §8.3 Corollary 1-3 (equality propagation and the universal large-degree formula)
Ch. 8 Problems 8.1 and 8.9: divisors and L(r(t)_0) on the projective line
Ch. 8 Problem 8.12: deg(D)=0 together with l(D)>0 is equivalent to D linearly equivalent to 0
Ch. 8 §8.1 Proposition 1 and Proposition 2: the divisor of a rational function has degree zero, linear equivalence is an equivalence relation, and degree is invariant
contents.reason: The degree-zero and linear-equivalence calculus is built on the batch-5 divisor page as thm-principal-divisor-degree-zero-proper-curve and its neighbours; this page only cites it and reproves nothing.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.3 Corollary 3: there is an integer N with l(D) = deg(D)+1-g for every divisor of degree greater than N
contents.reason: The universal degree threshold needs the duality identity i(D)=l(K-D); this page proves only the fixed-direction form cor-riemann-theorem-large-degree and the universal form is planned on the duality pair.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.3 Proposition 5 and Corollaries: the plane-curve computation of l(Em) and the genus formula via adjoints
contents.reason: The plane-curve arithmetic-genus formula is built on the curves pair as thm-plane-curve-arithmetic-genus; the adjoint-curve route is Fulton's classical proof device and is not re-scaffolded here.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.4 Lemmas 2-3 and Proposition 7: the universal derivation, one-dimensionality of Omega, and the DVR with local parameter
contents.reason: The differential and canonical-divisor machinery belongs to the duality pair, which carries def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point and the Serre-duality items; nothing on this page depends on it.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.5 Proposition 8 and Corollary: canonical divisors of plane curves, deg(W)=2g-2 and l(W)>=g
contents.reason: The identities deg K_C = 2g-2 and h^0(K_C)=g are exactly the duality pair's cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two and cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.6 Corollaries 2-3: deg(D)>=2g-1 gives l(D)=deg(D)+1-g, and deg(D)>=2g gives l(D-P)=l(D)-1 (base-point-freeness)
contents.reason: Both thresholds are consequences of the full Riemann-Roch theorem with duality and are planned on the duality pair as cor-rr-exact-high-degree-formula and thm-degree-two-g-line-bundle-basepoint-free.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.1 Residue theorem (adjoint form for plane curves with ordinary multiple points)
contents.reason: A classical plane-curve device for the Brill-Noether proof of Riemann-Roch through adjoints and residue conditions; this page proves the theorem by the Euler-characteristic route and uses neither adjoints nor multiple points.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 4: the preliminary estimate l(rZ) >= r·deg(Z) - tau for a nonconstant function x with zero divisor Z
contents.reason: A step in the classical field-theoretic proof of Riemann's theorem, superseded on this page by the derivation of the inequality from the Euler-characteristic Riemann-Roch identity; no scaffolded item needs the estimate.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.6 Corollary 4 (Clifford's theorem): l(D) <= (1/2)deg(D)+1 when l(D)>0 and l(W-D)>0
contents.reason: Clifford's inequality is a classical extra corollary of the full Riemann-Roch theorem with duality; no item of the scheme-theory curve track states or consumes it, so no item is scaffolded for it.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §§8.1-8.6 Problems 8.1-8.30 as a block (plane-curve examples, genus calculations, canonical divisors)
contents.reason: Fulton's problem sets develop the classical plane-curve route and its worked examples; the companion B page builds its own worked examples from the scaffolded items, so the problems receive no separate items.

read_evidence.method: The complete PDF (3,056,656 bytes) was downloaded and extracted to text; Sections 8.1-8.4 were read in full, in particular the torsion-free/locally-free criterion 8.1.1, the splitting lemmas 8.4.2 and 8.4.4, and Riemann-Roch version 1 (8.3.3).
read_evidence.scope: Chapter 8, Sections 8.1-8.4, all named results and their proofs

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.1 Lemma 8.1.1: on a smooth curve a finite module is locally free if and only if torsion-free, and a non-torsion-free module has a nonzero global section

Ch. 8 §8.2 Lemma 8.2.4: for an invertible module, the evaluation pairing is an isomorphism and every nonzero homomorphism into a locally free module is injective (used with the dual and tensor bookkeeping)
Ch. 8 §8.4 Theorem 8.4.1 (Birkhoff-Grothendieck): a finite torsion-free module on the projective line is a direct sum of twisting modules
Ch. 8 §8.4 Lemma 8.4.2: for large r there is no nonzero map O(r) -> M and h^0(M(-r)) = 0 (the maximal-twist step)
Ch. 8 §8.1 Lemma 8.1.20 and Corollary 8.1.19: dual sequences of locally free modules and biduality
Ch. 8 §8.4 Lemma 8.4.4: the quotient W in the twisted sequence has H^0(W(-1))=0, is torsion-free, and splits off a rank-one summand
Ch. 8 §8.3 Theorem 8.3.3 (Riemann-Roch, version 1): chi(O(D)) = chi(O) + deg(D) on a smooth projective curve
Ch. 8 §8.3 Corollary 8.3.8: chi(L) = deg(L) + 1 - p_a for an invertible module
Ch. 8 §8.3 Corollary 8.3.9: h^0(O(np)) tends to infinity with n, so functions with a single pole of large order exist
Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 8.2.7: O(D) tensor O(E) = O(D+E), O(D) dual = O(-D), and O(D) contained in O(E) if and only if E-D is effective
Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 8.2.10: every invertible module is isomorphic to O(D) for a divisor D (the Cartier-to-line-bundle dictionary in the smooth-curve case)
Ch. 8 §8.2 Proposition 8.2.12 and Corollary 8.2.13: maps O(D)->O(E) are multiplication by rational functions with div(f)+E-D effective, and O(D)=O(E) exactly for linearly equivalent divisors
Ch. 8 §8.2 Corollary 8.2.9: the maximal ideals of the structure sheaf correspond to divisors -D with D effective
Ch. 8 §8.3 Corollary 8.3.10: principal divisors have degree zero and linearly equivalent divisors have equal degrees

Ch. 8 §8.1 Lemmas 8.1.2-8.1.4, Corollaries 8.1.5, 8.1.8, 8.1.15, 8.1.17 and Propositions 8.1.7, 8.1.10: branched coverings, ideals as products of maximal ideals, local e-th root form, finiteness of Hom
contents.reason: The branched-covering dictionary is built on the curves pair (def-ramification-and-branch-points, lem-fibre-degree-sum-ramification-residue and the finite-map lemmas); this page uses only the resulting finite morphism C->P^1.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.3 Theorem 8.3.11: a smooth projective curve is a connected compact orientable surface in its classical topology
contents.reason: The classical-topology comparison is not used by the scheme-theoretic Euler-characteristic argument; the curves pair carries the geometric-genus comparison instead.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.1 Lemmas 8.1.13-8.1.14, 8.1.16: exactness of Hom and compatibility with localization
contents.reason: The sheaf-level Hom bookkeeping is already built on the divisor and cohomology pages of batches 5 and the published scheme infrastructure; no new item is created for it here.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.1 Notation 8.1.9: working on the base X with the direct image pi_*M
contents.reason: A notational convention for branched coverings, not a mathematical result; it has no item and no consumer on this page.

contents.name: Ch. 8 §8.4.1 equivalence with Birkhoff's 1909 matrix form and the historical remarks
contents.reason: Historical attribution rather than a separate mathematical statement; the mathematical content is covered by Theorem 8.4.1, which is scaffolded as thm-birkhoff-grothendieck-vector-bundles-p1.

read_evidence.method: The complete PDF (9,643,655 bytes) was downloaded and extracted to text; the Riemann-Roch section and the classification of vector bundles on P^1 with its exercises were read directly. Vakil's 2025 numbering places this material in Section 18.4-18.5; the design's citation to Chapter 21 is the older-edition numbering, recorded as locator drift in the batch notes.

contents.name: Ch. 18 §18.4.1: the Riemann-Roch theorem for line bundles on projective curves
Ch. 18 §18.4.4 and (18.4.4.1): arithmetic genus p_a = 1 - chi(O_C) and the restatement of Riemann-Roch in terms of it
Ch. 18 §18.4.2-18.4.3, 18.4.6-18.4.7: degree of a line bundle and of a coherent sheaf, and the degree map Pic -> Z as a homomorphism
contents.reason: The degree homomorphism on Pic is built on the batch-5 divisor page as cor-degree-descends-picard-curve and its neighbours; this page cites it as a supplier without restating it.

contents.name: Ch. 18 §18.5.1-18.5.2 (Serre duality for smooth projective varieties; the canonical bundle is dualizing) and Exercise 18.5.A(b): deg omega_C = 2g-2
contents.reason: Serre duality for curves and its consequences are the subject of the duality pair; this page deliberately proves the Euler-characteristic form without the duality identification.

contents.name: Ch. 18 §18.5.3 and 18.5.4: Riemann-Roch restated as h^0(L) - h^0(omega tensor L^dual) = deg L - p_a + 1, with the projective-line example omega = O(-2)
contents.reason: The dual restatement rewrites the index of speciality as a space of differentials; it is the first item of the duality pair and is not available on this page.

contents.name: Ch. 18 §18.5.6 Theorem (with the setup of §18.5.5): every vector bundle on P^1 is a direct sum of line bundles O(a_1)+...+O(a_r), uniquely up to ordering
Ch. 18 Exercise 18.5.C: uniqueness of the multiset of degrees, read off from h^0 of the twists
Ch. 18 Exercise 18.5.D: for m large negative Hom(O(m), E) is nonzero and for m large positive it vanishes, producing the maximal degree a_r
Ch. 18 Exercise 18.5.E: a nonzero map O(a_r) -> E is injective because O(a_r) is torsion-free
Ch. 18 Exercise 18.5.F: the cokernel of a maximal line subbundle is locally free, reducing the rank by one
Ch. 18 Exercises 18.5.G-18.5.H: the transition-matrix argument that puts an extension in upper-triangular form and splits it for rank two
Ch. 18 §18.5.7: the failure of splitting on P^n for n>1 and Horrocks' criterion
contents.reason: Higher-dimensional splitting criteria are not part of this pair; the curve-page classification stops at P^1 and no consumer on the scheme-theory curve track states Horrocks' theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 18 Exercise 18.5.I: finishing the Birkhoff-Grothendieck proof for arbitrary rank by induction
contents.reason: The induction's final bookkeeping is absorbed into thm-birkhoff-grothendieck-vector-bundles-p1 here; the rank-reduction lemmas it depends on are scaffolded on this page, and the exercise is listed against the duality pair only because that pair records the P^1 bundle classification as a downstream consumer.

contents.name: Ch. 18 §18.4.5 Miracle and §18.4.10-18.4.13: the complex-topology comparison, the universal conic example, and numerical equivalence of divisors
contents.reason: These are context and examples around the Riemann-Roch section rather than results used by this pair; the conic example concerns a different topic and numerical equivalence has no consumer here.

read_evidence.method: The complete PDF (745,082 bytes) was downloaded and extracted to text; the displayed statements and proofs of the linear-series section and of Riemann-Roch, the vanishing section, the very-ampleness lemmas and the genus section were inspected against the batch-7 inventory.

contents.name: §5 Lemma 5.1 (tag 0BS5): chi(X,O_X) = chi(X,omega^bullet) and chi(X,O_X) = -chi(X,omega_X) for Cohen-Macaulay one-dimensional X (used only as the source of the normalisation chi(O)=1-g)

§5 Lemma 5.2 (tag 0BS6, Riemann-Roch): for X proper, Gorenstein and one-dimensional, deg(omega_X) = -2chi(X,O_X) and chi(X,E) = deg(E) - (1/2)rank(E)deg(omega_X), with H^i(X,E) dual to H^{1-i}(X, E^dual tensor omega_X); the invertible rank-one Euler-characteristic content is chi(L) = deg(L) + chi(O_X)
§8 Definition 8.1 (tag 0BY7): the genus of a proper one-dimensional X with H^0(X,O_X)=k is g = dim_k H^1(X,O_X), agreeing with p_a = 1-chi(X,O_X)
§3 Definition 3.1 and Lemma 3.2 (tags 0CCN, 0CCP): linear series (L,V) of degree d and dimension r and the morphism to P^r they define when X is nonsingular
§3 Lemmas 3.3-3.5 and Remark 3.6 (tags 0CCQ-0CCT): restriction of linear series, the g^1_d morphism to P^1, and r <= d with equality implying genus zero
contents.reason: The linear-series toolkit is built on the curves pair (def-complete-linear-system, thm-base-point-free-linear-system-morphism, lem-function-with-poles-defines-map-p1); this page cites those as suppliers.

contents.name: §6 Lemmas 6.1-6.7 (tags 0BY5, 0B5D-0B5H): vanishing and global generation for twists of the dualizing module on a one-dimensional proper scheme
contents.reason: These are the duality-based vanishing statements for omega_X; this page's vanishing theorem is the fixed-direction Serre-vanishing argument and the omega-based refinement belongs to the duality pair.

contents.name: §7 Lemmas 7.1-7.2 (tags 0E8V-0E8W): L^{tensor 6} and L^{tensor 2} are very ample under regularity, vanishing and ampleness hypotheses
contents.reason: The very-ampleness thresholds are consumed by the duality pair's embedding corollaries (cor-projective-embedding-every-smooth-proper-curve and the degree-2g/2g+1 theorems), not by this page.

contents.name: §8 Lemmas 8.2-8.3 (tags 0BY9, 0C19): genus is invariant under field extension, and deg(omega_X) = 2g-2 for Gorenstein curves
contents.reason: The degree of the canonical bundle is the duality pair's cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two; the Euler-characteristic definition of the genus used here needs neither statement.

contents.name: §8 Lemma 8.4 (tag 0C1A): for a smooth proper curve, h^0(Omega_{X/k}) = g and deg Omega = 2g-2
contents.reason: The differentials and their degrees belong to the duality pair (def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point and the canonical items).

contents.name: §5 formulas (5.0.1)-(5.0.5) (tags 0BRX-0BS1): degree of a locally free module as chi(E) - rank(E)chi(O_X), first Chern class and the degree with respect to an ample bundle
contents.reason: The degree of an invertible sheaf and its compatibility with the divisor degree are built on the batch-5 divisor page; this page uses the resulting homomorphism deg: Pic -> Z through cor-degree-descends-picard-curve.

contents.name: §3 Lemma 3.5 equality case restated as 'equality r=d forces genus zero' and §5's discussion of fractions in the general Riemann-Roch formula
contents.reason: The textual discussion motivates the general Gorenstein statement whose rank-one part is scaffolded; the fractional-coefficient generality (Chow-homology form) is not used by any item of this pair.
